crossRefs.note: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Yah, and teach out of your law,
But when we are judged, we are punished by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening…
for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”
As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.
If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.
But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;
but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and…
Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.
Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.
For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,
For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in…
It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with children, for what son is there whom his father…

translations.web: My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his correction;
translations.bsb: My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe His rebuke;
translations.kjv: My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
translations.asv: My son, despise not the chastening of Jehovah; Neither be weary of his reproof:
